content: Clarithromycin is a semi-synthetic macrolide antibiotic. Chemically, it is known as 6-O-methylerythromycin. It appears as a white to off-white crystalline powder. This compound is soluble in acetone, slightly soluble in methanol, ethanol, and acetonitrile, and practically insoluble in water. The drug is marketed under the brand name Biaxin and is available in several formulations: immediate-release tablets, extended-release tablets, and granules for oral suspension. Each yellow, oval, film-coated immediate-release Biaxin tablet contains either 250 mg or 500 mg of clarithromycin. The 250 mg tablets include the following inactive ingredients: hypromellose, hydroxypropyl cellulose, croscarmellose sodium, D&C Yellow No. 10, FD&C Blue No. 1, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, povidone, pregelatinized starch, propylene glycol, silicon dioxide, sorbic acid, sorbitan monooleate, stearic acid, talc, titanium dioxide, and vanillin. The 500 mg tablets contain similar inactive ingredients, with the addition of colloidal silicon dioxide. Each yellow, oval, film-coated Biaxin XL tablet (extended-release formulation) contains 500 mg of clarithromycin. The inactive ingredients in this formulation include cellulosic polymers, D&C Yellow No. 10, lactose monohydrate, magnesium stearate, propylene glycol, sorbic acid, sorbitan monooleate, talc, titanium dioxide, and vanillin. After reconstitution, each 5 mL of Biaxin oral suspension contains either 125 mg or 250 mg of clarithromycin. The granules for oral suspension are available in bottles containing 1250 mg (50 mL size), 2500 mg (50 and 100 mL sizes), or 5000 mg (100 mL size) of clarithromycin. The inactive ingredients in the granules include carbomer, castor oil, citric acid, hypromellose phthalate, maltodextrin, potassium sorbate, povidone, silicon dioxide, sucrose, xanthan gum, titanium dioxide, and fruit punch flavor.
